title: Grafana — Unified Observability
description: Everything about Grafana on one board, in the pack's order: SLIs and SLOs, MTTD/MTTR and certification, policy and alerting, remediation, signals, pipeline, logs and traces.

options.content:
### Grafana · Unified Observability
One board in the pack's own order: SLIs and SLOs, the validation that proves them (MTTD, MTTR, certification, synthetic checks), policy and alerting, remediation, the signals underneath, the pipeline, logs and traces.  ·  pack `grafana@1.0.0`  ·  **Unified** · [Overview](/d/grafana-overview?${__url_time_range}) · [Alerting health](/d/grafana-alerting-health?${__url_time_range}) · [Plugins and auth](/d/grafana-plugins-and-auth?${__url_time_range}) · [Slo burn](/d/grafana-slo-burn?${__url_time_range})

panels.title: Http request success
panels.description: Fraction of HTTP requests returning non-5xx responses. Excludes intentional 4xx (auth failures, validation errors) by treating only 5xx as the failure class. SLO 99.9 % over 30d.

panels.title: Http request latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile HTTP request latency, server-side, across all handlers. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Datasource proxy success
panels.description: Fraction of datasource proxy requests (Grafana → Prometheus / Loki / Tempo / Elasticsearch / Influx etc.) that returned a non-5xx response. Failures here are the leading indicator that dashboards will break. SLO 99.5 % over 30d.

panels.title: Datasource proxy latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile datasource proxy request latency. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Database query latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile latency of Grafana's internal database queries (the metadata / dashboards / users / orgs store). Slow database queries directly degrade the UI and alerting evaluation. Prerequisite: grafana_database_queries_duration_seconds is exposed only with [database] instrument_queries = true (GF_DATABASE_INSTRUMENT_QUERIES), which is off by default; without it this SLI reads nothing. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Alerting rule evaluation success
panels.description: Fraction of unified alerting rule evaluations that succeeded vs. attempted. Failures here mean alerts FIRE-OR-NOT incorrectly and downstream notification reliability is undermined. SLO 99.95 % over 30d.

panels.title: Plugin request success
panels.description: Fraction of plugin requests (datasource and app plugins) that completed without error. Plugin failures often surface as broken panels before the plugin itself is suspected. SLO 99.9 % over 30d.

panels.title: Login success
panels.description: Fraction of form logins (POST /login) answered 200 in the window, from Grafana's own HTTP request histogram; a window with no login reads no data rather than NaN (the total leg keeps only series with a positive rate). Grafana also counts logins per client in grafana_authn_authn_successful_login_total{client} and grafana_authn_authn_failed_login_total{client} (both defined at 12.4.11; the failed one has no series until a login fails): that pair would also cover OAuth / SAML clients, but a failed login was not exercised in the lab while the HTTP pair was executed end to end (see the evidence). grafana_api_login_post_total counts successes only (per pkg/api/login.go). Scope: the login page (Grafana's own password path); OAuth and SAML callbacks are not in this ratio. Sudden drops mean Grafana's login path is failing and need fast triage even if signed-in sessions still work. SLO 99.9 % over 7d.

panels.title: Error-budget burn · last hour
panels.description: 1 h error-budget burn rate per SLO: 1× consumes the budget exactly over the SLO window; amber at the smallest factor that alerts for that SLO, red at the largest (spec.policy).

panels.title: Burn rate · 5 m window
panels.description: Fast window: reacts within minutes; pages when both it and the slow window exceed the factor. Hover for per-SLO values.

panels.title: Burn rate · 1 h window
panels.description: Slow window: keeps burning for up to an hour after an incident by design.

options.content: The pack declares 4 chaos experiments (chaos-mesh; staging) but no certification pipeline — a scrape job named `certification` — so nothing feeds MTTD, MTTR or a verdict here.

| Check | Kind | Target | Interval | Assertions | On fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grafana-api-canary` | blackbox-exporter | `https://grafana.internal/api/health` | 30s | status_code=200; latency_lt=500ms; body_contains="database":"ok" | SEV1 |
| `grafana-login-canary` | k6 | `https://grafana.internal/login` | 5m | login_success=true; session_cookie_set=true | SEV2 |
| `grafana-dashboard-render` | grafana-synthetics | `https://grafana.internal/d/obs-overview` | 5m | render_complete=true; panel_errors=0 | SEV2 |

<small>Declared in the pack's `validation.synthetic_checks`; the pack module supplies the panels that show the probes' own metrics.</small>

targets.expr: count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", pack="grafana", burn_rate="", kind=""}) or vector(0)

panels.title: Symptom alerts · pending / firing
panels.description: State of every symptom alert of the pack over the time range.

targets.expr: (2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="grafana", alertstate="firing", burn_rate="", kind=""})) or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="grafana", alertstate="pending", burn_rate="", kind=""}) or label_replace(vector(0), "alertname", "no alert", "", "")

panels.title: Firing pack alerts
panels.description: Everything currently firing with the pack label, most severe first.

panels.title: Burn-rate & forecast alerts · pending / firing
panels.description: Multi-window burn-rate alerts (fast windows page, slow windows linger after incidents) and forecasts.

targets.expr: (2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="grafana", alertstate="firing", burn_rate!=""})) or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="grafana", alertstate="pending", burn_rate!=""}) or label_replace(vector(0), "alertname", "no alert", "", "")
(2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="grafana", alertstate="firing", kind="forecast"})) or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="grafana", alertstate="pending", kind="forecast"})

options.content:
| Trigger | Runbook | Automation (declared) | Guardrails (declared) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grafana-http-5xx-burn` | `runbooks/grafana-http-errors.md` | `restart-grafana-pod-rolling` | ≤ 2/h · human above SEV1 · cooldown 15m |
| `grafana-datasource-proxy-burn` | `runbooks/grafana-datasource-down.md` | `reload-datasource-config` | ≤ 3/h · human above SEV2 · cooldown 10m |
| `grafana-database-latency-burn` | `runbooks/grafana-database-slow.md` | `grafana-database-vacuum` | ≤ 1/h · human above SEV2 · cooldown 6h |
| `grafana-login-success-burn` | `runbooks/grafana-idp-outage.md` | `manual-only` | ≤ 1/h · human above SEV1 |

<small>Automations and guardrails come from the pack's `remediation` section for the platform to implement; in this lab every action is done by hand, as the runbooks say.</small>
